full_judgment: 8. We have consideration the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the judgment of the both the court's below and the evidence on record. It is not denied that suit land belonged to Jamuna Prosad Saha. The plaintiff claims title by purchase from Jamuna Prosad Saha on the basis of registered kabala dated 25-3-63 Exhibit 1. The plaintiff has filed the kabala in original which was marked Exhibit 1 without any objection. The registered kabala of over 30 years old is not required to be proved by examining scribe and attesting witnesses when it is marked exhibit without objection. This registered kabala dated 25-3-63 has a presumption of genuineness and correctness in the execution and registration of the kabala and this presumption could not be rebutted by the contesting defendant. We do not therefore find any reason as to why this registered kabala should not be accepted as genuine document. We therefore, disagree with the finding of the lower appellate Court that the kabala Exhibit 1 is not admissible in evidence and we conclude that the kabala Exhibit 1 is very much admissible and the plaintiff acquired title to the suit land on the basis of kabala Exhibit 1. This was also the finding of the trial Court.
